title: Sampled golden-sweep curation and access matrix for config-triggered regressions
creator: Riley Chen
description: Problem: Config and model changes (quantization, kernel swaps, routing policies) are periodically causing subtle quality regressions that escape broad evals because the golden dataset sampling is stale or insufficiently scoped. Proposal: run automated, timeboxed 'golden sweeps' that sample across strata (few-shot vs zero-shot, long-context, code, safety buckets) and maintain a lightweight curation/access matrix so stewards can sign off, revoke, or expand sweeps quickly. Deliverables include: (1) a repeatable sampled-sweep pipeline that produces signed snapshot manifests, (2) an access matrix and signer rotation workflow for curators, (3) a small 'rollback playback' harness that can reproduce failures locally from a snapshot, and (4) CI gating hooks that fail config/model PRs when regressions exceed thresholds. This ticket coordinates engineering pieces and finalizes the access model and manifest format. See design brief: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Sampled+Golden+Sweep+Proposal and prototype runner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-ci/pull/189
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible pipeline exists that can create a sampled golden sweep snapshot for a given model/config with deterministic sampling seed and metadata
Snapshot manifest includes stratification labels, sampling seed, signer id, timestamp, and an immutable hash; manifests are stored in S3 and referenced by unique id
Curator access matrix implemented: team owners, read-only roles, emergency revoke flow, and signer rotation docs; tested for at least two teams
Rollback playback harness can take a snapshot id and replay the same prompts against a specified runtime variant locally or in a sandbox cluster
CI gating integration added: PRs that change runtime config/model routing run the sampled-sweep job and post results; PR status blocks when regression delta > configured threshold
Runbook for investigating sweep regressions (triage checklist, dashboards, alert contacts) is published in Confluence
tasks: Design and agree manifest schema (fields: snapshot_id, hash, seed, strata_breakdown, signer, signed_at, acl_ref)
Implement sampled-sweep runner service (Docker + k8s job) with deterministic sampler and stratification config
Add signer flow: ephemeral key signing for snapshots + rotation schedule; integrate with KMS
Build lightweight playback harness to replay a snapshot against runtime variants (local CLI + sandbox job)
Wire sampled-sweep into CI: a lightweight job triggered for PRs touching config/model routing that posts an artifact link and summary status
Create access matrix UI/CSV and a script to grant/revoke access for curator groups
Write Confluence runbook, add dashboards (per-snapshot delta metrics) and alerting rules
comments: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to limit initial sweep size to 3k prompts across 5 strata to keep cost low. Action: Diego to prototype sampler (Riley to draft manifest schema).

2026-02-26: Prototype sampler implemented. Deterministic seeding chosen over strict stratified quotas to ensure reproducible sampling for CI. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-ci/pull/189

2026-03-02: Security reviewed signer model options. Decided on KMS-backed ephemeral signing keys with 30-day rotation to balance auditability and operational complexity. Follow-up ticket for rotation automation planned.

2026-03-08: Design review with PM and stewards. PM asks for per-customer opt-outs for private datasets — flagged as out of scope for initial sweep, will surface as product work (PM-110500? placeholder).

2026-03-12: Integration trade-off: running full sweep in PR is expensive. Team agrees to synthetic smoke sweep in PR (100 prompts) then schedule full sweep async and post results; gating uses async results + threshold windows.

2026-03-14: Implemented manifest schema and basic signer integration in branch eng/feature/sampled-sweeps. Next: playback harness and CI hook. Linked branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-ci/tree/eng/feature/sampled-sweeps
